title: Backdating created_at reaches the health snapshot only after a reindex
body:
Call store.reindex() after the backdated putAtom. upsertAtom's ON CONFLICT clause updates every column except created_at, so a memory that already has an index row keeps its original date and loadHealthSnapshot reports the wrong age. The rebuild reads the git file, which is where the truth is.

Why: created_at is immutable identity and the index enforces that. Without the rebuild an age test passes or fails for a reason unrelated to what it claims to measure.

evidence.summary: upsertAtom ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE sets updated_at but never created_at
seedEffective calls db.reindex() after the backdated putAtom for exactly this reason
Anchored delivery: keywords validated against this memory's own text and a generic-request corpus before proposing.

issues: archived_by_person: describes the v1 sqlite index (upsertAtom)

v1.trigger: when a test backdates a memory's created_at to exercise an age threshold, such as dead_inferred or retirement
